items.headline: Sweeney praises Bane's leadership, Suggs' offseason effort
items.summary: Sean Sweeney said he made a point of meeting individually with every player this offseason. He called Desmond Bane leadership and team personified and cited Jalen Suggs' commitment, saying the roster has shown different things and it is his job to blend it together.

items.headline: Magic sign Kevin Knox II to Exhibit 10 deal
items.summary: Knox, the No. 9 pick in 2018, joins training camp on an Exhibit 10 deal and will wear No. 24. He averaged 22.7 points, 8.2 rebounds and 2.5 assists for Windy City in the G League last season. Unlike four other Exhibit 10 signees this week, he was not waived same-day; the camp roster stands at 20.

items.headline: Magic sign and waive four to lock up G League rights
items.summary: Orlando signed Ace Baldwin Jr., Ricky Council IV, Jarron Cumberland and Au'Diese Toney to Exhibit 10 deals and waived all four the same day, securing their returning-player rights for Osceola. Baldwin and Cumberland played for Osceola last season; Council and Toney came over in trades for their G League rights.

items.headline: Cain, Penda and Bitadze fighting for their jobs in camp
items.summary: Jamal Cain's $2.6M salary is non-guaranteed. Goga Bitadze projects as the third center behind Carter Jr. and Vucevic. Penda is viewed as the long-term defensive forward off the bench.

items.headline: Magic Youth Foundation commits $1.8M for 2026-27
items.summary: The first $775K goes to 21 Central Florida nonprofits, with a second round in Feb 2027. The foundation also launched the OMYF Collective for nonprofit leaders.

items.headline: Season preview: getting Franz and Suggs healthy is priority one
items.summary: Wagner played 34 games last season and Suggs 57. The preview names Anthony Black a breakout candidate and flags 3-point shooting and a defensive slide from 2nd to 13th.

items.headline: DAZN pricing set for Magic games
items.summary: Standard: $19.99 a month or $119.99 a season. Ultimate: $24.99 a month or $139.99 a season. 7-day free trial in the Magic's territory, 20% off for season-ticket holders.

items.headline: Preseason power rankings: Ringer 15th, Yahoo 19th
items.summary: The Ringer has Orlando 15th overall and 9th in the East. Kevin O'Connor at Yahoo has them 19th and 11th in the East, citing 3-point shooting.

items.headline: Banchero details summer work with Kevin Durant
items.summary: Footwork, shotmaking, post-ups and finishing at game speed with trainer Adam Harrington. Banchero called it the hardest he has worked in an offseason.

items.headline: Five position battles facing Sweeney
items.summary: Starting center (Carter Jr. vs Vucevic), Penda vs da Silva, Nelson vs Isaac, Jase Richardson vs Jevon Carter, and whether Suggs keeps the starting point guard job over Black.

items.headline: Magic drop to 21st in ESPN's three-year outlook
items.summary: They were 7th a year ago. ESPN cites five players earning over $20M, luxury-tax pressure and no playoff series win for the Banchero-Wagner core.

items.headline: Osceola Magic hire Ronnie Burrell as head coach
items.summary: The 2023 G League Coach of the Year and former Blazers and Nets assistant replaces Dylan Murphy. Osceola opens Nov 8.

items.headline: Osceola trade for Ricky Council IV's returning-player rights
items.summary: Osceola sent Phillip Wheeler's rights and a 2027 G League first-round pick to Rio Grande Valley.

items.headline: Still no Anthony Black extension
items.summary: The deadline is Oct 19. Keyonte George's 5-year, $157.5M deal is the comparable most cited. Reports conflict on whether a deal is likely.

items.headline: Banchero and Franz trade talk is speculation, not reporting
items.summary: A Bleacher Report trade idea and a Nets podcast drove the chatter. No insider has reported talks.

items.headline: Jokic names Wendell Carter Jr. among his toughest defenders
items.summary: On a Serbian podcast, Jokic listed Jalen Duren and Carter Jr. as smaller centers who are tough to deal with.

items.headline: Magic reportedly wanted John Konchar before he signed with the Knicks
items.summary: Single-source report with no reporter named. Orlando is keeping its 15th roster spot open.

items.headline: STUFF named 2026 NBA Mascot of the Year
items.summary: His third win, after 2016 and 2017.

items.headline: Camp's three big stories: shooting, da Silva, Black and Suggs
items.summary: Banchero is a 31.7% career 3-point shooter and Franz 32.4%. Improvement has to come from within.

items.headline: Banchero: last season was the most difficult of his career
items.summary: On the Internal Reps podcast he called it a frustrating year for him and the organization, and said it propelled him toward the player he will be.

items.headline: Franz Wagner and Jonathan Isaac listed questionable for start of season
items.summary: CBS's injury page lists Wagner (calf) and Isaac (knee) as questionable and Izaiyah Nelson (ankle) out until at least Nov 1. No team statement yet.

items.headline: Branham and Davison sign Exhibit 10 deals
items.summary: Malaki Branham (2022 No. 20 pick) and JD Davison (2024-25 G League MVP) join camp on non-guaranteed contracts.

items.headline: Media day and camp schedule set
items.summary: Media day Sept 28 at 11 AM. Camp runs Sept 29 to Oct 6 at the AdventHealth Training Center, off Oct 3.

items.headline: DAZN named exclusive streaming partner
items.summary: DAZN carries all non-national games in the Magic's territory. Orlando is the fifth NBA team on DAZN.

items.headline: Gray Media deal adds free games in North Florida
items.summary: About 70 games on WTGB (Gainesville), WJHG (Panama City) and WCTV (Tallahassee).

items.headline: WMOR 32 will carry every non-national game in Tampa
items.summary: Up from 10 games last season. Broadcast crew: Dante Marchitelli, Jeff Turner and Kendra Douglas.

items.headline: Bitadze scores 23 as Georgia routs Montenegro
items.summary: 23 points, 8 rebounds and 2 blocks in a 101-74 World Cup qualifier win.

items.headline: Da Silva plays World Cup qualifiers for Germany
items.summary: Scored 5 in a 99-83 win over the Netherlands. Germany then won in overtime at Poland.

items.headline: Bane says Sweeney flew to Texas to visit him
items.summary: Bane: talent is not the problem, it is about collective buy-in. He called the visit a sign of Sweeney's commitment.

items.headline: John Beilein joins as senior coaching consultant
items.summary: The former Michigan coach will assist Sweeney. The two worked together in Detroit.

items.headline: 2026-27 schedule released
items.summary: Opener Oct 21 vs Atlanta. 8 national TV games, 14 back-to-backs, finale Apr 11 at Miami. NBA Cup group: Toronto, Milwaukee, Brooklyn, Detroit.

items.headline: Banchero on his partnership with Franz Wagner
items.summary: The two worked out together in Los Angeles this summer. Banchero compared the duo to Tatum and Brown.

items.headline: Magic games move to free over-the-air TV
items.summary: Cox Media Group deal: WRDQ TV 27 (now MagicTV 27) carries all local games and WFTV 9 select games. Replaces FanDuel Sports Network Florida, which shut down.

items.headline: Franz Wagner skips Germany's summer to get healthy
items.summary: He passed on the Supercup and World Cup qualifiers. In July he said the plan was to not play at all and focus on getting fully healthy.

items.headline: David Steele retires after 37 seasons
items.summary: The longtime TV voice of the Magic retired. Dante Marchitelli takes over play-by-play.

items.headline: Izaiyah Nelson fractures ankle at Summer League
items.summary: The two-way rookie had surgery with a 3-4 month timeline.

items.headline: Sweeney's coaching staff finalized
items.summary: Joe Prunty stays. Additions include Greg Buckner, Popeye Jones, Ben Johnson, Mfon Udofia and D.J. Bakker. Jacqlyn Poss and Shannan Lum are the team's first female assistant coaches.

items.headline: Moritz Wagner signs with Brooklyn
items.summary: Two years, $19M with the Nets.

items.headline: Vucevic returns to Orlando on a one-year deal
items.summary: The former Magic All-Star signed for the minimum. Jevon Carter and Jonathan Isaac also re-signed.

items.headline: Magic waive Jonathan Isaac to save money
items.summary: Waived one day before his $14.5M salary guaranteed, leaving $8M in dead money. He re-signed on a minimum deal July 1.

items.headline: Magic trade back and take Izaiyah Nelson at No. 51
items.summary: Orlando sent No. 46 to Washington for Nos. 51 and 60, then sent No. 60 to Milwaukee for cash.

items.headline: Sean Sweeney formally introduced
items.summary: The former Spurs associate head coach was introduced after San Antonio's Finals run ended.

items.headline: Magic fire Jamahl Mosley
items.summary: Fired after five seasons and a first-round loss to Detroit in which Orlando led 3-1. Jeff Weltman said the team needed a fresh voice.
